title: Late labs and excused absences
summary: No late labs. One make-up path for excused absences, run by email.

la: Send late-lab and absence questions to email

nodes.text: No answer at the desk: email the Lab
Graded with the batch; then closed

sections.title: The rule
sections.text: Labs close at 5:00 PM on the due date. Late work isn't accepted, technology problems included. The one routine exception is an Excused Absence, and telling the Lab is the student's job.

sections.title: Lab assistant
list: Don't approve, promise or reopen anything.
Say: "Please email {email} by 5:00 PM on the 2nd business day after the due date. You don't need your approval yet."
Don't ask why and don't accept medical records.
Grading: every lab not turned in by 5:00 PM gets 0, even if the student emailed. See [Grading lab videos](#/grading/missing).

sections.title: What the student does
steps: Emails the Lab by 5:00 PM on the 2nd business day after the due date (or before, if they know ahead).
Submits the lab and forwards the Dean of Students' email by 5:00 PM, 7 days after the due date.

sections.title: Coordinator
list: Send the standard reply; don't ask why.
Reopen the lab with Bongo and quiz special access.
Grade it with that lab's batch and replace the lab assistant's 0. Nothing is graded after the close.
Told on time but the Dean's email came late, or the absence ran past the close: exempt the lab. One per student per course.
Bongo or D2L down for everyone, or a campus closed: extend for all sections with one announcement.
Accommodations: work with SAS and the professor directly.
